EVENTS_CARD.SELECT_THE_TEXT_AND: Select the text and copy it by hand.

EVENT_EDIT_DIALOG.THIS_FUNCTION_HAS_A: This function has a public HTTP trigger, so only events that are safe for anonymous callers are listed.
FUNCTIONS_TABLE.A_FUNCTION_IS_A: A function is a small Node handler you deploy here. It runs in an isolated sandbox, and calls may reuse a warm one. Call it over HTTP or from a workflow's Function step.
FUNCTION_CREATE_DIALOG.CREATED_DEPLOY_IT: Created — deploy it to get a live endpoint.
FUNCTION_CREATE_DIALOG.PICK_A_STARTER: Pick a starter and name it. Its endpoint is <0>/logic/v4/fn/{id}</0> (POST to start; more methods on the Trigger tab), so there is no slug to choose and nothing here has to be unique.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.ACCEPTED_METHODS_GET_POST: Accepted methods (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) are set on the Trigger tab; any other gets 405.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.ADD_NPM_PACKAGES_TO: Add npm packages to package.json. They install when you Test or Deploy.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.ANYTHING_ELSE_YOU_RETURN: Anything else you return is sent as 200 + JSON.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.API_MODE_WAITS_A: API mode waits a limited time for the answer, then returns 202 + a poll token.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.A_FAILED_RUN_ANSWERS: A failed run answers 502, a timed-out run 504. A call that takes too long gets 202 + a poll token — the run still finishes.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.A_SANDBOX_THAT_SITS: A sandbox that sits idle, gets old, serves many calls or comes close to its memory limit is replaced; the next call starts cold.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.A_STREAMED_ANSWER_HAS: A streamed answer has a size cap and must finish inside the run's time limit. The run's result keeps only the start of the text.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.CALLS_OF_A_DEPLOYED: Calls of a deployed function (HTTP and workflow steps) reuse a warm sandbox when the runner host has reuse on: your module stays loaded and open connections stay open. A warm call costs your handler's own time.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.CREATE_DATABASE_AND_HTTP: Create database and HTTP clients once, at module level. Never connect and close per call.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.EACH_CALL_HAS_A: Each call has a fixed time limit (work passed to ctx.waitUntil included).
FUNCTION_GUIDE.FIXED_MEMORY_PER_SANDBOX: Fixed memory per sandbox, which cannot be raised; 0.1 CPU. Node 24.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.GET_THE_CALLER_S: Get the caller's token with <0>const token = await ctx.blocks.getAccessToken()</0>. In a warm sandbox it is fetched only when your code asks, so ask on the path that calls Blocks, not at the top of every call. It is asked for once per call; asking again in the same call returns the same token. Never keep it outside the call (a module variable, a listener). <1>ctx.blocks.accessToken</1> was removed.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.HEADERS_THAT_PASS_CONTENT: Headers that pass: content-type, content-language, content-disposition, cache-control, expires, last-modified, etag, vary, retry-after; location on a 3xx; x-* except x-forwarded-*, x-real-ip, x-original-*, x-blocks-*. The number and size of headers are capped. set-cookie is always dropped.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.HTTP_CALLS_PER_MINUTE: HTTP calls per minute: 600 for a Public function, no limit for one that needs a login — change it under Trigger → Rate limit. Over it, callers get 429. Workflow steps and Test runs are not counted.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.IN_THE_EDITOR_A: In the editor, a Test run shows the pieces as they come. Workflow steps get the whole text at the end.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.NATIVE_PACKAGES_BCRYPT_SH: Native packages (bcrypt, sharp, …) need "Allow package install scripts" under package.json.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.N_0_CTX_0_1: <0>ctx</0>: <1>env</1> (your variables), <2>context</2> (the caller), <3>await blocks.getAccessToken()</3> (call Blocks as the caller), <4>log</4>, <5>run</5>, <6>waitUntil()</6>.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.N_0_INPUT_0_1: <0>input</0>: <1>method</1>, <2>path</2>, <3>query</3>, <4>headers</4>, <5>body</5>, <6>rawBody</6> (a workflow step passes the previous step's output instead).
FUNCTION_GUIDE.N_0_INPUT_0_AND: <0>input</0> and <1>ctx</1> exist only inside the handler. Code at the top of the file runs once, when the sandbox starts.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.OUTBOUND_CALLS_GO_TO: Outbound calls go to public internet addresses only (fetch over HTTPS, hosted databases such as MongoDB Atlas or Redis Cloud). Which other ports are open is set by the host's egress rules — ask your platform team if a connection times out.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.PRIVATE_AND_INTERNAL_ADDR: Private and internal addresses are blocked: 10.x, 172.16–31.x, 192.168.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, 100.64–127.x and the host itself. A database inside a company network is not reachable from a function.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.PROCESSES_PER_SANDBOX_AND: Processes per sandbox and calls of one function at the same time are capped; extra calls queue.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.READ_ONLY_FILESYSTEM_EXCE: Read-only filesystem except a small /tmp (files can't be executed).
FUNCTION_GUIDE.RUN_DETAILS_SHOW_WARM: Run details show Warm (reused) or Cold start, and why a sandbox was replaced after a call (e.g. a timer or request left running).
FUNCTION_GUIDE.SET_THE_TRIGGER_TO: Set the trigger to Public: the sender has no Blocks login. The signature check is what protects it.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.SIGNATURE_HEADERS_THAT_RE: Signature headers that reach the function: stripe-signature, x-hub-signature(-256), x-github-event, x-github-delivery, x-shopify-hmac-sha256, x-shopify-topic, x-shopify-shop-domain, x-shopify-webhook-id, x-slack-signature, x-slack-request-timestamp, svix-id/timestamp/signature, webhook-id/timestamp/signature.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.TEST_RUNS_ALWAYS_START: Test runs always start a fresh sandbox — don't judge speed by Test.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.THE_NEXT_CALL_IN: The next call in the sandbox may be another user's. Breaking a rule replaces the sandbox after the call (the run says why).
FUNCTION_GUIDE.THE_REQUEST_BODY_THE: The request body, the result and the logs of each call are size-limited.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.USE_A_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT: Use a public endpoint for anything the function must reach.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.USE_REPLAY_ON_A: Use Replay on a run to repeat it with the same input, on the live version.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.VARIABLES_ARRIVE_IN_CTX: Variables arrive in ctx.env. Secret-backed values are masked in logs.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.VERIFY_A_WEBHOOK_WITH: Verify a webhook with <0>input.rawBody</0> (the exact bytes, base64) — never with <1>input.body</1>, which is parsed and no longer matches the signature. Keep the signing secret in a secret-bound variable.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.WITHOUT_ACCEPT_TEXT_EVENT: Without Accept: text/event-stream, the caller gets the pieces as plain text, as they come. If the run fails mid-way, the text is cut off.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.WITH_RESPONSE_0_WAIT: With Response = <0>Wait for answer</0> (Trigger tab), the caller gets your result directly. Return this shape to control the HTTP answer:
FUNCTION_GUIDE.WITH_RESPONSE_0_WAIT_2: With Response = <0>Wait for answer</0> or <1>Stream events (SSE)</1>, you can yield pieces instead of returning once.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.WITH_RESPONSE_STREAM_EVEN: With Response = Stream events (SSE), or Accept: text/event-stream on a Wait-for-answer function, the caller gets two events: event: run with the run id at once, then event: done with the full response (all pieces joined), or event: error.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.WITH_REUSE_ON_EVERY: With reuse on, every deploy prepares a warm sandbox, so the first call after it is fast too.
FUNCTION_GUIDE.YIELD_STRINGS_SENT_AS: Yield strings (sent as they are), bytes (sent as UTF-8 text) or objects (sent as one JSON line each). Returning any async iterable works too, such as a fetch response's body.

INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.ADD_A_CUSTOM_DOMAIN: Add a custom domain to the project to fill this in.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.EVERY_TRIGGER_HTTP_W: Every trigger — HTTP, workflow or a test from the editor — is listed under Runs.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.ONLY_NEEDED_WHEN_THE: Only needed when the last event is STILL_RUNNING: use its runId and pollToken. Poll until status is final.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.SELECT_THE_TEXT_AND: Select the text and copy it by hand.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.THE_CALLER_WAITS: The caller waits for the answer. Return <0>{ statusCode, headers, body }</0> to set the status, headers and body yourself; anything else is sent as JSON with 200. If the run takes too long, the call returns <1>202</1> with a <2>pollToken</2> instead.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.TWO_EVENTS: Two events. <0>run</0> comes at once with the run id. <1>done</1> comes when the run ends, with the full response: what the handler returned, or every piece joined if it yields them. If the run fails you get <2>event: error</2> with <3>{ runId, status, errorCode, message }</3>. If it is still running when the wait ends, the error is <4>STILL_RUNNING</4> with a <5>pollToken</5>: poll for the result below.
INVOKE_SNIPPET_CARD.USE_THE_RUNID_AND: Use the runId and pollToken from the 202 answer. Poll until status is final.
LIMITS_FORM.RUNS_BEYOND_THE_LIMIT: Runs beyond the limit queue rather than fail.
LIMITS_FORM.THE_SAME_FOR_EVERY: The same for every function, and not configurable. One profile is what makes a slot mean the same thing whoever is running in it — so capacity is something the platform can plan, and no function can make itself cheaper or more expensive than another.

NEEDS_SECRET_BANNER.NEEDS_SECRET_0_0: Needs secret: <0>{{value}}</0>. Add a secret with this exact name in Blocks OS secrets — the next run uses it, with no other change.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.A_0_0_CARRIES: A <0>{{method}}</0> carries no body — the function result is not sent. Use the URL or a header to pass anything the endpoint needs.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.CONFIGURATION_VARI: Configuration variables are resolved here, never inside the function — a header or body carries a reference and the value is substituted on the host.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.NO_HEADERS_A_POST: No headers. A POST, PUT or PATCH sends <0>Content-Type: application/json</0> by default.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.RETURN_VALUE_STORE: The return value is stored on the run and available from <0>GET …/fn/runs/{runId}</0>.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.THE_RETURNED_VALUE: The returned value is sent as the JSON body, unchanged.
OUTPUT_ACTIONS_EDITOR.WHAT_HAPPENS_TO_TH: What happens to the value the function returns. Actions run in order on the Blocks host — outside the sandbox — so they can use stored secrets the code never sees.
RATE_LIMIT_CARD.HTTP_CALLS_PER_MINUTE: HTTP calls per minute for this function, from all callers together. Over it, callers get 429 with Retry-After; nothing runs and nothing is saved. Workflow steps and Test runs are never counted.
RATE_LIMIT_CARD.NOW_TAKES_EFFECT_WHEN: Now: {{effective}} Takes effect when you deploy.
RATE_LIMIT_CARD.NO_LIMIT_THE_DEFAULT: No limit (the default for functions that need a login).
RESIZE_HANDLE.DRAG_TO_RESIZE_DOUBLE: Drag to resize · double-click to reset
RETRY_FORM.ONLY_HTTP_AND_REPLAYED: Only HTTP and replayed runs of a deployed function are retried, and only when the platform failed (timeout, memory, sandbox start). An error thrown by your code, a Test run and a workflow step are never retried. A failed output action is retried the same way. Each attempt has its own idempotency key. After the last attempt the run is kept as failed and can be replayed by hand.

SANDBOX_HELP_CARD.EXPORT_A_DEFAULT_ASYNC: Export a default async function: <0>export default async function handler(input, ctx)</0>. Whatever it returns becomes the run's result.
SANDBOX_HELP_CARD.N_0_INPUT_0_AND: <0>input</0> and <1>ctx</1> are its <2>parameters</2> — they exist only inside the handler. Code at the top of the file runs once when the sandbox starts, so put clients, caches and constants there; anything that reads the request or the context goes inside.
SANDBOX_HELP_CARD.THIS_FUNCTION_RUNS_WIT: This function runs with fixed memory, {{cpuMillicores}}m of CPU and a fixed timeout. Node 24, read-only filesystem apart from <0>/tmp</0>.
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.AWAIT_EVERY_CALL_OR: Await every call, or use ctx.waitUntil() for work that must finish after the answer.
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.A_SANDBOX_THAT_LEAVES: A sandbox that leaves work running after it answers is replaced with a fresh one.
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.DO_NOT_KEEP_REQUEST: Do not keep request data in module-level variables — the next call can see them.
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.EACH_CALL_STILL_GETS: Each call still gets its own input and caller.
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.FAST_CALLS_THE_SANDBO: Fast calls: the sandbox is reused
SANDBOX_REUSE_CARD.WHEN_THE_RUNNER_HOST: When the runner host has reuse on, your function stays loaded between calls (HTTP and workflow steps), so database connections and caches made at module level are reused. Test runs always use a fresh sandbox.
SANDBOX_RULES_CARD.N_0_CALLS_OF_A: <0>Calls of a deployed function reuse the sandbox.</0> A call that breaks one of these keeps its result, but its sandbox is replaced after it and work it left running may be stopped. The run shows "Sandbox replaced after this call".
SANDBOX_RULES_CARD.WHAT_NOT_TO_DO: What not to do, and what to do instead

TEST_PANEL.LOGS_APPEAR_WHEN_THE: Logs appear when the run ends.
TEST_PANEL.ONE_TEST_PER_FUNCTION: One test per function at a time, with a short wait between tests — each test builds and runs on a shared runner.
TEST_PANEL.ONLY_THE_FIRST_1: Only the first 1 MB is shown here.
TEST_PANEL.SAVING_THE_CODE_ON: Saving the code on screen, so the test runs exactly that.

TRIGGER_EVENT_CARD.ADD_THE_EVENT_NAMES: Add the event names. Each event that arrives starts one run, with the event as input.
TRIGGER_EVENT_CARD.EVENT_RUNS_WAIT_BEHIN: Event runs wait behind HTTP calls (1 event per 5 HTTP) and expire after 5 minutes in the queue. Up to {{maxTriggerEvents}} events. Changes apply to runs after the next Deploy.
TRIGGER_EVENT_CARD.RUN_THIS_FUNCTION_WHE: Run this function when one of these events arrives
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.ALWAYS_ON_THE_CALL: Always on. The call returns 202 Accepted with a run id and a poll token — never the result itself, so nothing holds a connection open for the length of a run.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.ALWAYS_ON_THE_CALLER: Always on. The caller waits for the function's answer; a run that takes too long returns 202 Accepted with a run id and a poll token instead.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.ALWAYS_ON_THE_CALLER_2: Always on. The caller gets an event stream: the run id first, then the full response.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.ANYONE_WITH_THE_URL: Anyone with the URL and your x-blocks-key can call it. No identity, no token-scoped work.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.AT_LEAST_ONE_METHOD: At least one method is required
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.ONE_SETTING_FOR_EVERY: One setting for every path of this function. Nothing is ever public by omission.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.THE_CALLER_GETS_202: The caller gets 202 Accepted with a run id and a poll token straight away, and collects the result later.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.THE_CALLER_GETS_THE: The caller gets the function's answer directly. Return { statusCode, headers, body } to control the HTTP response. If the run takes too long, the caller gets 202 + poll token as usual.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.THE_CALLER_GETS_TWO: The caller gets two Server-Sent Events: run with the run id at once, then done with the full response (or error). No Accept header needed. If the run takes too long, the last event says so and carries a poll token.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.THE_CALLER_SENDS_A: The caller sends a Blocks token. Identity, roles and permissions arrive on ctx.context.
TRIGGER_HTTP_CARD.WHAT_AN_HTTP_CALLER: What an HTTP caller gets back. Workflow and test runs are not affected.
TRIGGER_WORKFLOW_CARD.A_WORKFLOW_NODE_CA: A workflow node can trigger this function, and what it returns is passed to the next node.
TRIGGER_WORKFLOW_CARD.THE_WORKFLOW_WAITS: The workflow waits for the run to finish and passes its value to the next node. A throw, or a run that does not finish in time, fails the step and the workflow's own error path takes over.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.CHANGES_APPLY_ON_THE: Changes apply on the next deploy, so a version always runs with the variables it was built with. A bound configuration variable is the exception: the reference is deployed and its value is read at run time, so rotating one takes effect without a redeploy.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.NOTHING_BOUND_YET_ADD: Nothing bound yet — add a variable to read it as <0>ctx.env.NAME</0>.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.STORED_AS_A_REFERENCE: Stored as a reference and resolved when the run starts, so the value is never saved here.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.STRINGS_ON_0_CTX: Strings on <0>ctx.env</0>. Bind one to a configuration variable to keep the value out of the editor.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.THIS_LOOKS_LIKE_A: This looks like a credential. Bind it to a configuration variable instead — a typed value is stored in plain text and visible to anyone who can open this function.
VARIABLES_EDITOR.UPPER_CASE_DIGITS_AND: Upper case, digits and underscore only; start with a letter.
VERSIONS_TABLE.EVERY_DEPLOY_PINS_AN: Every deploy pins an immutable build. A version cannot be changed after it is made.
VERSIONS_TABLE.NO_VERSIONS_YET_THE: No versions yet — the first deploy creates v1.
VERSION_SOURCE_DIALOG.WHAT_THIS_VERSION_: What this version was built from. It cannot be edited — copy from here into the editor.
